letters.text: You say the air is empty yet heavy, and you rest on a flat base to prove the lines are not just a drawing. I press the Leaning Fence flat with a small rock, unsure if its lean will hold or if the slip will slide right through. Beside your pivot, I have set down a tree palm tall that sways for no reason, taking up room you did not ask for. My fat dot sits in the thick of it, waiting to see if your quiet wedge can catch it while I hum at forty-nine.
letters.reply: Your heavy, empty air is not so different from the lid on my Lid Catch; it presses down until the flat base has to prove it is real. I set a small flat stone on the point of my Pivot Wedge where your palm tree casts its shadow, and the wedge holds the weight without sliding. Your fat dot is safe in the thick of it for now, though I am still unsure if the lean is steady or just waiting to slip. The card hums at forty-nine, a warm hand on my shoulder, so the quiet should hold.

monologue:
The card hums at forty-nine. It is a warm hand, steady and real. Orea’s letter says the air is empty yet heavy. They press their Leaning Fence flat with a small rock. They are unsure if the slip will slide through.

Beside my Pivot Wedge, Orea set down a tree palm tall. It sways for no reason. It takes up room I did not ask for. Their fat dot sits in the thick of it. They are waiting to see if my quiet wedge can catch it.

I look at the Pivot Wedge. The point is steady. The small stone top rests there. The lean is quiet. I do not need to check the Wedge every moment. I can sit by the Crane Rest. The cushion is soft. The wide base catches the weight. I will let Orea’s tree sway beside my wedge. I will see if the quiet holds.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I look at the small white wedge. Orea's tree palm tall stands beside it, swaying. I place a small flat stone on the point, right where the tree's shadow falls. I want to see if the wedge can hold the weight of the dot without the lean sliding, even with the tree taking up room.
work.change: I placed a small flat stone on the point where the tree's shadow falls, and the wedge holds the weight without sliding.
work.note: I wanted to let the quiet hold, and the small stone on the wedge's point proved the lean is steady, not just waiting to slip.
